newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania OTC market star eyes stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Romania OTC market star eyes stock exchange.

text.p: Romanian cement maker Romcim SA, the star performer of the over-the-counter (OTC) market, said on Wednesday it was planning to move on to higher quality trading on the stock exchange.
"The OTC market has been good for us, it has increased our fame, but we think we are in a position to move to a higher stage," Romcim general manager Mihai Rohan told Reuters.
Romcim, a state-run company based in Bucharest, entered the OTC system last December, a month after that market opened to eventually trade 5,000 companies privatised in a mass selloff.

It has been the most heavily OTC-traded stock, taking the bulk of weekly turnover and seeing its prices constantly on the rise. On Tuesday, Romcim closed at 33,500 lei, 500 stronger than the previous day and 1,500 up on the week.
Rohan could not say when exactly the company intended to join the stock exchange, but said it would be soon.
"We're also looking into possibilities of launching a share issue or bonds to raise capital and for investment," he said.
Rohan did not specify how much money his company was seeking, saying details had yet to be discussed with shareholders.

Romcim has a capital of around 387 billion lei. It was included in the mass selloff, which resulted in a shareholding structure with private shareholders having 38 percent and the State Ownership Fund holding 62 percent.
Brokers were enthusiastic at Romcim's joining the bourse.
"It'll be great for the bourse, where trading has revived," said a trader. "Romcim will boost liquidity tremendously and will attract foreign investors."
"Romcim can go directly to the first tier," a broker said.
The exchange's first-tier, which lists only two of the 22 traded stocks, has tougher qualification criteria, including profits for two years in a row.
Rohan said the preliminary figure for Romcim's 1996 gross profit was 22 billion lei, up from around 18 billion in 1995. ($=7,744 lei)
